title: Regulatory obligation heatmap + rapid-reply orchestrator for customer questionnaire exceptions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build an adaptive triage playbook and lightweight engine that maps incoming vendor/customer questionnaire items to a prioritized regulatory obligation heatmap, produces a candidate evidence bundle, and surfaces a recommended SLA and remediation estimate. This ticket captures the PM scope: decision heuristics, acceptance criteria, stakeholder list, initial mapping taxonomy, and rollout plan.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-response for high-volume questionnaire lanes by 60%.
- Produce defensible SLA/commitment recommendations for enterprise accounts based on risk, data residency, and product footprint.
- Provide a ranked list of required controls and evidence with estimated effort and owner.

Out of scope:
- Full automation of legally-significant contract clauses (handled by Legal).
- Deep technical remediation work (handled under separate engineering tickets).

Acceptance criteria (must all be met):
1) For a set of 150 historical questionnaire items, the triage engine correctly assigns a regulatory tag (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/GDPR/DPA) at >=90% precision.
2) The system returns a candidate evidence bundle (links to docs, config screenshots, audit artifacts) for 70% of items.
3) The recommended SLA band (Fast/Standard/Negotiation) matches historical routing decisions in 85% of sampled cases.
4) UX: PM triage playbook is published to Confluence and a 30-minute training session is run with Solutions and Security.

Proposed flow:
1) Intake: Questionnaire arrives via Support/SE/Portal and is tagged with account sensitivity signals (customer-enterprise-tier, data residency, regulated industry).
2) Parse: NLP classifier extracts question intent and maps to canonical obligations (e.g., encryption-at-rest, SOC2-CC6.1, DPA-data-subprocessors).
3) Heatmap: Combine obligation severity, account sensitivity, and implementation gap to compute a heat score (0-100).
4) Orchestrator: Recommend one of three outcomes: Fast Reply (existing evidence), Evidence Assemble (requires cross-team pull), Escalate to Legal/Account Exec. Provide an estimated hours-to-fulfill and recommended SLA band per outcome.
5) Output: Create a draft reply template + attach candidate evidence links and assign owners.

Mapping taxonomy (initial):
- Technical controls: encryption, network segmentation, backups, logging
- Process controls: incident response, DR, vendor management
- Data residency & transfers: cross-border, subprocessors
- Privacy obligations: data subject rights, retention, DPIAs

Metrics to track post-launch:
- Mean time to first response (by SLA band)
- Fraction of items with auto-suggested evidence accepted by PM/SE
- False positive/negative rates for obligation classification
- Support load reduction (tickets handled without legal/engineering intervention)

Trade-offs and constraints:
- High recall classifier risks giving too many false assurances; we prioritize precision for automated suggestions and route low-confidence items to human review.
- Evidence bundle confidence degrades across older docs; we will mark provenance and timestamp on every suggested artifact.
- Data residency signals rely on external account metadata; must integrate with Account DB (dependency noted).

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- Security: Leah O'Connor (review mapping rules)
- Legal: Daniel Ruiz (review escalation buckets)
- Solutions/SE: Priya Nambiar (UX and reply templates)
- Engineering: Dima Koval (integration scope and API contract)

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (pilot): Run classifier against 150 historical questionnaires; manual review to build mappings and tune thresholds.
- Week 2: Implement Confluence playbook and reply templates; run internal alpha with Solutions team.
- Week 3: Beta with 10 enterprise customers and feedback loop; instrument metrics.
- Week 4: Iterate and propose release for console-2025.03 (limited feature flag).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Incorrect mapping could create contractual exposure. Mitigation: All auto-suggested bundles are labeled as 'Suggested — verify with Security/Legal' until confidence threshold and manual audit pass.
- Risk: Engineering bandwidth for Account DB integration. Mitigation: Provide a degraded mode that uses account tags provided in intake form.

Next steps:
- Align on canonical obligation taxonomy with Security (due 2025-03-15).
- Kickoff discovery call with Solutions and Legal (scheduled 2025-03-13).
- Create ENG spike for classifier evaluation (ENG-4521).
